title: Finite constant torsors on the closed subscheme are trivial
statement: Let R be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with separably closed fraction field [def-pc-separably-closed], and let Z be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] of Spec R [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every finite abelian group M, every torsor [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors] under its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on Z is equivariantly isomorphic to the trivial torsor.

proof.text: Apply Scheme.EtaleTorsor.exists_toSheafTorsor_equiv to represent T by a finite etale surjective scheme torsor t. This uses finite local constancy of a constant finite-group torsor, the existing finite locally constant representability theorem, and transport of the action by Yoneda.

Put X = Spec R. Identify its function field with FractionRing R using the fraction-ring algebra equivalence and transfer IsSepClosed along its ring equivalence. Scheme.isIntegrallyClosed_stalk_Spec supplies normality of the stalks, while integrality supplies their domain instances. Closed immersions and finite morphisms are affine, so both Z and t.P are affine.

Apply the section clause of exists_finite_clopen_opens_and_section_of_closedImmersion to i and t.pi, using the torsor fields giving etaleness, finiteness and surjectivity. This gives s with s composed with t.pi equal to the identity.

Use nonempty_toSheafTorsor_sheaf_obj_iff at the terminal object of the small etale site to obtain a global section of the represented torsor, and nonempty_iff_of_equiv to transport it to T. Restrict the chosen section x to every object U and send a section a of the constant group sheaf to T.vadd U a x_U. The restriction identity map_map_apply and map_vadd prove naturality. The identity add_vadd proves equivariance, so Torsor.Iso.ofHom turns this morphism from the trivial torsor into an isomorphism; its inverse proves the required relation.
